name: Kingdom of Macedon (Alexander III)

areaKm2.note: Educated guess. Analogue: the modern Greek region of Macedonia (~34,000 km2) plus Upper Macedonia/Paeonia; high adds directly ruled parts of Thrace. Seshat (https://seshat-db.com/core/polity/506) codes only 10,000 km2 for 359 BCE, the core before Philip II's expansion.

population.note: Seshat codes the Macedonian polity at 1,000,000 for 359-336 BCE (single value; range is ours). Macedon proper (Lower and Upper Macedonia, Chalcidice, east to the Nestos) only: Thessaly, Thrace and the League of Corinth members are not counted, although their contingents are in `forces`.

urbanization.note: Educated guess: a mostly rural kingdom; Pella, Aigai, Pydna, Amphipolis were the main towns (Seshat largest settlement 20,000-80,000 for 330-312).

activePersonnel.note: Field and home armies (50,600) + League fleet crews and engineers (34,000) + margin. About half are non-Macedonians: League allies (7,000 infantry, 600 cavalry, the fleet), Greek mercenaries (5,000) and Balkan contingents (7,000+).

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess: Macedonians trained under Philip but not under arms; reinforcements of a few thousand were sent to Asia in 333.

supportPersonnel.note: League fleet 160 triremes x ~200 crew = 32,000 (largely allied Greeks) + ~2,000 engineers, surveyors (bematists), staff.

mobilizationRatio.note: Analogy with the Greek total-war call-up of 90% of the year classes 20-49/55 in 480 (Hansen 2006, https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 10), slightly lower for a less urbanised kingdom.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Diodorus 17.17.3-5 as accepted by Bosworth, Conquest and Empire (1988), Part II section on the army, and Hammond & Walbank, A History of Macedonia III (isbn:0198148151): crossing army 32,000 infantry + 5,100 cavalry; Antipater kept 12,000 infantry + 1,500 cavalry in Europe. Parmenion's advance force (~10,000 in 336, Polyaenus 5.44.4) is only in the high value because it may already be inside Diodorus' totals. Line = Macedonian phalanx and hypaspists (12,000) + League hoplites (7,000) + mercenary hoplites (5,000) + Antipater's 12,000.

quality.note: Sarissa phalanx and hypaspists the era's best (1.0); allied and mercenary hoplites era-typical (0.5).

training.note: Philip's professionalised Macedonian infantry (0.75-1.0); allies citizen militia (0.5).

count.note: Diodorus 17.17.3-5 as accepted by Bosworth, Conquest and Empire (1988), Part II section on the army, and Hammond & Walbank, A History of Macedonia III (isbn:0198148151): crossing army 32,000 infantry + 5,100 cavalry; Antipater kept 12,000 infantry + 1,500 cavalry in Europe. Parmenion's advance force (~10,000 in 336, Polyaenus 5.44.4) is only in the high value because it may already be inside Diodorus' totals. Odrysians, Triballians, Illyrians (7,000) + Agrianians (~500).

quality.note: Javelinmen; the Agrianians were elite skirmishers.

count.note: Diodorus 17.17.3-5 as accepted by Bosworth, Conquest and Empire (1988), Part II section on the army, and Hammond & Walbank, A History of Macedonia III (isbn:0198148151): crossing army 32,000 infantry + 5,100 cavalry; Antipater kept 12,000 infantry + 1,500 cavalry in Europe. Parmenion's advance force (~10,000 in 336, Polyaenus 5.44.4) is only in the high value because it may already be inside Diodorus' totals. Cretan and Macedonian archers (~500, shared 1,000 with the Agrianians).

Diodorus 17.17.3-5 as accepted by Bosworth, Conquest and Empire (1988), Part II section on the army, and Hammond & Walbank, A History of Macedonia III (isbn:0198148151): crossing army 32,000 infantry + 5,100 cavalry; Antipater kept 12,000 infantry + 1,500 cavalry in Europe. Parmenion's advance force (~10,000 in 336, Polyaenus 5.44.4) is only in the high value because it may already be inside Diodorus' totals. Companions 1,800 + Thessalians 1,800 + allied Greek cavalry 600 + Antipater's 1,500.

quality.note: Companion and Thessalian shock cavalry, the era's best (rubric 1.0).

count.note: Diodorus 17.17.3-5 as accepted by Bosworth, Conquest and Empire (1988), Part II section on the army, and Hammond & Walbank, A History of Macedonia III (isbn:0198148151): crossing army 32,000 infantry + 5,100 cavalry; Antipater kept 12,000 infantry + 1,500 cavalry in Europe. Parmenion's advance force (~10,000 in 336, Polyaenus 5.44.4) is only in the high value because it may already be inside Diodorus' totals. Thracian and Paeonian prodromoi/scouts 900.
Arrian 1.11.6: 160 triremes of the League fleet (ancient figure accepted by modern historians; low/high are +/-~12% for uncertainty). Disbanded after Miletus in 334.

quality.note: Standard triremes; inferior to the Persian-Phoenician fleet.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 1.0 row (best-in-era command): Alexander, with Parmenion and Philip's trained officer corps; mid 0.9 at the start of the campaign.

cohesion.note: Macedonian units 0.75-1.0 (regional taxeis, Companions); allied and mercenary contingents lower.

morale.note: Rubric 0.75: motivated, recent victories (Chaeronea 338, Balkan campaign and Thebes 335).

weapons.note: Anchor 3 exactly (300 BCE: iron weapons, torsion artillery, sarissa).

ships.note: Anchor 3: triremes; no larger polyremes in the League fleet.

fortification.note: Anchor 3: siege towers and torsion artillery (Philip at Perinthus 340, Diades' engineers).

logistics.note: Anchor 3: Engels (isbn:0520042727) shows minimal baggage, soldiers carrying their own rations and pack horses instead of wagons, and pre-arranged depots.

communications.note: Mounted couriers; no permanent relay system until the Persian one was taken over.

isr.note: Year anchor 3: prodromoi scouts, bematists surveying routes.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 via https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true: Greece year 1 CE = 1,275 (2011 int$). Macedon was less urbanised than southern Greece but rich in timber, horses and Pangaion gold.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess: a permanent army on Philip's model; Alexander crossed to Asia in debt (Arrian 7.9.6 / Plutarch, ancient).

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: mining (Pangaion), timber and shipbuilding, crafts.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess: fertile plains of Emathia and Thessaly; self-sufficient in grain.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in an ancient Greek-type age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model used for all classical snapshots.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: some military roads built under Philip II; no engineered network.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess: timber and grain coasting trade; the League's merchant shipping (Athens) is not counted.

supplyRangeKm.note: Engels (ch. 1-2): the army carried its own provisions on soldiers and pack animals and could operate only a limited number of days from water and a supply source; mid assumes ~1 week of marching between depots or the fleet.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: ~0.06-0.1 horses, mules and oxen per inhabitant x population (horse-rich kingdom).

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.1: familiar mountain terrain and local supply; few fortified cities.

notes: Snapshot = spring 334 BCE, Alexander crossing the Hellespont. Border "none": historical-basemaps has no Macedon polygon near this date. world_bc400 is not available, world_bc323 shows only the "Empire of Alexander" (after the conquests), and world_bc500 lumps Macedon into the shared "Greek city-states" polygon (which also includes southern Greece, Magna Graecia and Massalia). Population is Macedon proper only; League of Corinth allies, Thessalians, mercenaries and Balkan troops are in `forces` but their homelands are not counted (includes = []). Army figures are Diodorus' breakdown as accepted by modern historians; Arrian gives "not much more than 30,000 infantry and over 5,000 cavalry". The siege train (torsion artillery) is not counted: its size at the start is undocumented.
